_comment: Shared entry/documents/logistics data, rendered by the `entry` macro in src/itinerary.njk, filtered per trip by main.json `countries: [...]`. Regulatory facts verified July 2025 with sources listed per country. ETIAS date/fee are VOLATILE — wording is hedged; re-check the official EU link before travel.

albania.name: Albania
albania.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond arrival is the stated rule; carry ≥6 months to be safe. Albania is NOT in the Schengen Area, so time here does not count against the Schengen 90/180 clock.

etias.status: Not applicable — Albania is outside the EU/Schengen zone, so no ETIAS is required to enter Albania.
etias.note: ETIAS only ever applies to the Schengen side of this trip (the Corfu, Greece buffer night). If ETIAS is live by Jun 2027 you'd need one €20 authorization for the Greece leg; if it hasn't launched, no action. Confirm on the official EU site close to departure.

albania.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free, and unusually generous: up to 1 year of stay per entry under a US–Albania bilateral agreement (far beyond the 90 days you'll use).
albania.idp: Your US license is accepted for non-resident stays, but carry a 1949-Geneva-Convention IDP (AAA, ~$20) — car-rental desks and police checkpoints routinely ask for it.
albania.driving: Drive on the right. Rentals skew manual — book an automatic early and expect a premium. Min age ~21 (under-25 surcharge common). Mountain roads (SH21 to Theth) are now mostly paved but narrow with steep drop-offs; the SH8 Riviera coast road is winding. Defensive driving essential — local habits are aggressive.
albania.tolls: One tolled stretch (the Rrëshen–Kalimash 'Nation's Highway' tunnel road toward Kosovo, not on this route). Otherwise effectively toll-free; pay the tunnel toll in cash/card if you ever take it.

money.cards: Cards accepted in city hotels/restaurants and larger coastal spots; mountain guesthouses, small cafés, ferries, and parking are frequently CASH ONLY.
money.cash: Currency is the Albanian lek (ALL); ~90–100 lek per USD. Euros are sometimes taken on the coast but at a poor rate — use lek. Withdraw lek from ATMs (choose 'without conversion' to dodge DCC fees); carry cash for Theth.
money.tipping: Not obligatory; rounding up or ~5–10% in cash is appreciated for good service.

albania.water: Tap water is chlorinated in cities but locals largely drink bottled; in Theth and rural areas stick to bottled or filtered. Bottled water is very cheap.
albania.emergency: 112 (unified EU-style emergency number, works nationwide). Also 129 police / 127 ambulance / 128 fire.
albania.esim: Airalo or Holafly Albania eSIMs work well; buy before departure. Coverage is good on the coast and in Tirana, patchy deep in the Theth valley.

sources.label: US State Dept — Albania travel info
Albania MFA — visa regime for foreigners

portugal.name: Portugal (incl. Madeira)
portugal.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond your planned EU departure, and issued within the last 10 years.

etias.status: Expected to launch late 2026 (repeatedly delayed — not yet confirmed).
etias.fee: €20 (confirmed Jul 2025, subject to change; under-18s and over-70s exempt).
etias.note: ETIAS is a pre-travel authorization for visa-free visitors incl. US citizens. Timeline has slipped several times — confirm on the official EU site close to departure. If it isn't yet live for Jun 2027, no action is needed.

portugal.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free up to 90 days per 180.
portugal.idp: Recommended, not legally required. Get one from AAA before you go; some rental insurers ask for it.
portugal.driving: Rental fleet is mostly manual — book an automatic early and expect a premium. Min age ~21; under-25 surcharge ~€6–15/day.
portugal.tolls: Electronic tolls (Via Verde). Rentals usually include a transponder (~€1–2/day + tolls); confirm toll handling when booking.

money.cash: Carry €50–100 — small cafés and family spots may be cash/Multibanco only.
money.tipping: Not expected; 5–10% appreciated for good service (cash).

portugal.water: Safe in Lisbon and most cities. Algarve tap can taste earthy (hard water) — bottled if sensitive.
portugal.esim: Holafly or Airalo Eurolink work well; buy before departure.

sources.label: US State Dept — Schengen passport rules

greece.name: Greece (Crete)
greece.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond your planned EU departure, and issued within the last 10 years.

etias.status: Expected to launch late 2026 (repeatedly delayed — not yet confirmed).
etias.fee: €20 (confirmed Jul 2025, subject to change; under-18s and over-70s exempt).
etias.note: ETIAS is a pre-travel authorization for visa-free visitors incl. US citizens. Timeline has slipped several times — confirm on the official EU site close to departure. If it isn't yet live for Jun 2027, no action is needed.

greece.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free up to 90 days per 180.
greece.idp: Strongly recommended — Greek insurers may require both a US license and an IDP. Get one from AAA before you go.
greece.driving: Rental fleet is mostly manual — book an automatic early. Min age ~21; under-25 surcharge ~€6–15/day.
greece.tolls: Motorway tolls (GRITS network). Pay cash (EUR) at booths or use a rental e-pass transponder.

money.cards: Cards accepted in cities, hotels and tourist tavernas.
money.cash: Carry €100–200 — remote villages and some island spots are cash-only in practice.
money.tipping: 10–15% for good restaurant service; round up casual bills (cash).

greece.water: Athens/mainland excellent; Crete tap is safe but very hard (chalky). Some smaller islands need bottled.
greece.esim: Holafly or Airalo Eurolink work well; buy before departure.

sources.label: US State Dept — Schengen passport rules

italy.name: Italy (Sicily)
italy.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond your planned EU departure, and issued within the last 10 years.

etias.status: Expected to launch late 2026 (repeatedly delayed — not yet confirmed).
etias.fee: €20 (confirmed Jul 2025, subject to change; under-18s and over-70s exempt).
etias.note: ETIAS is a pre-travel authorization for visa-free visitors incl. US citizens. Timeline has slipped several times — confirm on the official EU site close to departure. If it isn't yet live for Jun 2027, no action is needed.

italy.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free up to 90 days per 180.
italy.idp: Strongly recommended and widely expected; helps with insurance. Get one from AAA before you go.
italy.driving: Rental fleet is mostly manual — book an automatic early. Min age ~21; under-25 surcharge ~€5–25/day.
italy.tolls: Autostrada tolls — pay by card at booths (avoid Telepass-only lanes), or rent a Telepass device (~€5–8/day + tolls).
italy.ztl: ZTL limited-traffic zones cover historic centers and are camera-enforced (€80+ fines by mail). If your lodging is inside one, register your plate with the host; otherwise park outside and walk.

money.cash: Carry €100–150 — trattorias, markets and rural spots may be cash-only.
money.tipping: Optional; round up or 5–10% for good service.

italy.water: Safe throughout Italy incl. Sicily; can be hard/chalky but fine to drink.
italy.esim: Holafly or Airalo Eurolink work well; buy before departure.

sources.label: US State Dept — Schengen passport rules

malta.name: Malta
malta.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond your planned EU departure, and issued within the last 10 years (Malta is in the Schengen area).

etias.status: Expected to launch late 2026 (repeatedly delayed — not yet confirmed). Applies to Malta as a Schengen state.
etias.fee: €20 (confirmed Jul 2025, subject to change; under-18s and over-70s exempt).
etias.note: One ETIAS authorization covers the whole Schengen area, so the same approval used for Italy also admits you to Malta — no separate application. Confirm on the official EU site close to departure; if it isn't live for Jun 2027, no action is needed.

malta.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free up to 90 days per 180 (shared Schengen allowance with Italy).
malta.idp: Recommended, not legally required for US licenses. Get one from AAA; some rental insurers ask for it.
malta.driving: Malta drives on the LEFT — cars are right-hand-drive. Roads are narrow, hilly and signage is patchy; drivers are assertive and roundabouts are constant. If you can avoid a car on the main islands (taxis/ferries/buses cover most of it), do. Rentals are cheap (~€25–40/day) but nerve-wracking for first-time left-side drivers.

money.cards: Cards accepted almost everywhere; contactless is standard.
money.cash: Carry €50–100 for the Gozo/Comino boats, village kiosks and market stalls.

malta.water: Tap water is safe but heavily desalinated and tastes of minerals — most visitors (and locals) drink bottled; bring a filter bottle if you dislike the taste.
malta.esim: Same Holafly/Airalo Eurolink eSIM used for Italy covers Malta — no new plan needed. English is an official language, so support is easy.

sources.label: US State Dept — Schengen passport rules

spain.name: Spain (incl. Mallorca)
spain.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond your planned EU departure, and issued within the last 10 years.

etias.status: Expected to launch late 2026 (re-check before June 2027).
etias.note: ETIAS is a pre-travel authorization for visa-free US visitors to Schengen countries. If launch slips again before June 2027, no action is needed.

spain.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free up to 90 days per 180.
spain.idp: Recommended with a US license for rentals; carry passport, license, IDP, and rental paperwork together.
spain.driving: Right-side driving. Mallorca roads are generally easy, but Tramuntana and Formentor routes are narrow and seasonal access rules can change.
spain.tolls: No island toll-road system like mainland Portugal; budget for parking, blue-zone meters, and possible beach/natural-park lots.
spain.ztl: Avoid driving into old-town Palma, Valldemossa, Soller, and Alcudia cores unless lodging confirms access and parking.

money.cards: Cards widely accepted in hotels, restaurants, supermarkets, and activity desks.
money.cash: Carry €50–100 for beach parking, small cafes, market snacks, and tips.
money.tipping: Not required; rounding up or 5–10% for strong service is appreciated.

spain.water: Tap water is safe; bottled water may taste better because island tap water can be hard or desalinated.
spain.esim: Airalo Eurolink, Holafly Europe, or a carrier roaming pass should cover Spain and Portugal on one plan.

france.name: France (Corsica)
france.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond your planned EU departure, and issued within the last 10 years.

etias.status: Expected to launch late 2026 (repeatedly delayed — not yet confirmed).
etias.fee: €20 (confirmed Jul 2025, subject to change; under-18s and over-70s exempt).
etias.note: ETIAS is a pre-travel authorization for visa-free visitors incl. US citizens. Timeline has slipped several times — confirm on the official EU site close to departure. If it isn't yet live for Jun 2027, no action is needed.

france.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free up to 90 days per 180.
france.idp: Strongly recommended — a US license is valid for short stays, but carry an IDP as an official translation; some rental agencies require it. Get one from AAA before you go.
france.driving: Rental fleet is mostly manual — book an automatic early. Corsica's roads are narrow, steep and winding; drive unhurried. Min age ~21; under-25 surcharge ~€5–25/day.
france.tolls: No toll motorways on Corsica — the island has no autoroute network, only toll-free N/D roads. (Mainland France uses péage autoroutes, paid by card or a Bip&Go tag.)

money.cards: Cards accepted in hotels, restaurants and shops.
money.cash: Carry €100–150 — village cafés, small beaches and markets can be cash-only.
money.tipping: Service is included (service compris); round up or leave 5–10% for good service.

france.water: Tap water is safe throughout Corsica and mainland France.
france.esim: Holafly or Airalo Eurolink work well; buy before departure.

sources.label: US State Dept — Schengen passport rules
France.fr — renting a car and driving in France

iceland.name: Iceland
iceland.passportRule: Valid ≥3 months beyond your planned Schengen departure, and issued within the last 10 years. Iceland is in the Schengen Area, so time here counts against the 90/180 clock.

etias.status: Expected to launch late 2026 (repeatedly delayed — not yet confirmed). Applies to Iceland as a Schengen state.
etias.fee: €20 (confirmed Jul 2025, subject to change; under-18s and over-70s exempt).
etias.note: ETIAS is a pre-travel authorization for visa-free visitors incl. US citizens. Timeline has slipped several times — confirm on the official EU site close to departure. If it isn't yet live for Jun 2027, no action is needed.

iceland.visa: None for US citizens — visa-free up to 90 days per 180.
iceland.idp: A US license is accepted for short stays; an IDP is recommended (cheap translation) and some rental insurers ask for it. Carry passport, license, IDP, and rental paperwork together.
iceland.driving: Drive on the right; rentals default to automatic (still book early for June). Min age ~20 (under-25 surcharge common). The SW/South route needs no F-roads or 4x4, but roads are windy, gravel shoulders are loose, and single-lane bridges (einbreið brú) require yielding. Headlights must be ON 24/7 (midnight sun makes this easy to forget). Off-road/off-track driving is illegal and heavily fined. Hold the car door against the wind — wind damage is the #1 rental claim, and gravel/sand-ash (SAAP/GP) insurance is worth it on the south coast.
iceland.tolls: Effectively toll-free on this route. The Hvalfjörður tunnel (near Reykjavík) is now free; the only toll road is Vaðlaheiðargöng in the north (not on this itinerary, paid online within 3 hours if used).

money.cards: Iceland is nearly cashless — contactless cards work everywhere, including gas pumps, parking, and remote guesthouses. A card with a PIN is essential for unattended fuel pumps.
money.cash: You barely need any. Currency is the Icelandic króna (ISK), ~135–140 ISK per USD. Skip the currency exchange; a fee-free card covers everything.
money.tipping: Not expected or customary — service is included. Rounding up for exceptional service is welcome but never required.

iceland.water: Tap water is glacial, free, and among the best on Earth — always drink from the tap, never buy bottled. Cold tap is odourless; HOT tap water is geothermal and smells faintly of sulfur (rotten-egg) — that's normal and harmless, just use cold for drinking.
iceland.emergency: 112 (single number for all emergencies; the 112 Iceland app can send your GPS location to rescue teams — install it).
iceland.esim: Airalo, Nova, or Síminn eSIMs work well; buy before departure. Coverage is strong along the whole SW/South ring-road corridor; expect dead zones only in the highlands (not on this route).

sources.label: SafeTravel.is — official Iceland road & safety alerts

usa.name: USA (Hawaii)
usa.passportRule: N/A — domestic. A valid government photo ID (REAL ID) is required to fly; passports optional.
usa.idp: N/A — US license valid in all states.
usa.driving: US rentals default to automatic. Min age typically 21 (varies by company/state).
usa.tolls: Minimal on the islands; rental toll programs charge any tolls to the card on file.
usa.water: Tap water safe throughout Hawaii (EPA standards).
usa.esim: Not needed — use your normal US cell plan.
